selected.rationale: Loss on WebApp->Ordering.API hits a known no_timeout synchronous checkout call, so the order-placement request can hang to the client deadline and expose missing timeout/retry defenses on the most critical business path.
Delay on WebApp->Ordering.API propagates unbounded latency into the confirmed no-timeout ordering call, stalling order submission and revealing the lack of a per-request timeout or circuit breaker.
Loss on WebApp->Catalog.API targets another statically confirmed no_timeout edge, causing catalog browsing to hang and exposing the same missing timeout defense on a synchronous user-facing path.
Delay on WebApp->Catalog.API is not absorbed by any timeout, so slow catalog responses directly stall WebApp requests and demonstrate unbounded latency propagation on a high-traffic edge.
Loss on WebApp->Basket.API, a core cart/checkout dependency, will likely hang the synchronous request due to the same HttpClient timeout pattern, causing cart and checkout availability loss.
Delay on WebApp->Basket.API can stall cart and checkout operations without client-side degradation, exposing a probable missing per-request timeout or fallback on a critical business edge.
Loss on Mobile BFF->Ordering.API breaks mobile order placement and, without a downstream timeout or retry, can hang mobile clients; this is high-impact on the checkout flow.
Delay on Mobile BFF->Ordering.API can make mobile order submission hang to the client deadline, exposing missing timeout/circuit protection on the mobile ordering edge.
